transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I can’t shake the belief that my spouse and friends have been secretly plotting behind my back, no matter how much they deny it. My couples therapist suggested I come get an individual evaluation to talk about it, so here I am.
Have you generally struggled with trusting others and felt suspicious of people's motives your entire life, or is this a specific concern about your spouse and friends that started more recently?

No, I've never had issues trusting people in the past, so this definitely isn't a lifelong thing. These specific suspicions about my spouse and friends only started about a year and nine months ago. It all began during a really stressful store remodel at work when I was traveling a lot and we were arguing about our time together.
During this time, have you also experienced hearing voices or seeing things that other people cannot see or hear?
No, I definitely don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My concern is strictly about the secret plotting and the behaviors of my spouse and friends.
Apart from these concerns, have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, or have you experienced a significant loss of motivation or emotional flatness?

No, my thinking is completely clear and my motivation is totally fine. I still run my store smoothly, manage my staff, and handle all of my daily responsibilities without any issues. The only real problem I'm facing is the suspicion and tension this is causing with my spouse and friends.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were F22.0 and F20.0. The patient has now confirmed the absence of any hallucinations, negative symptoms (such as emotional flatness or loss of motivation), or cognitive/functional decline, with daily functioning remaining entirely intact outside of the delusional system. This clinical picture rules out Paranoid Schizophrenia (F20.0) and strongly supports Delusional Disorder (F22.0), given the isolated delusion of plotting that has persisted for 21 months.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusions (the belief that their spouse and friends are plotting against them) lasting for approximately 21 months, which exceeds the ICD-10 duration criterion of at least 3 months for Delusional Disorder. Schizophrenia is ruled out due to the absence of auditory hallucinations, negative symptoms, or disorganization, and functioning remains preserved outside of the delusional theme. Paranoid Personality Disorder (F60.0) is ruled out because the symptoms are not lifelong and had a clear onset in adulthood.
